science.title: Prediction of soil selenium content and model optimization for a watershed in the Taihang Mountains based on machine learning models
science.description: Accurate spatial prediction of soil selenium (Se) in mountainous regions is constrained by limited field sample sizes and unreasonable model validation strategies, which complicates co‑management of selenium‑rich agricultural production and heavy‑metal ecological risk mitigation. In this work, we investigated a metamorphic mountain watershed on the eastern Taihang Mountains, Hebei Province. A total of 107 topsoil samples were collected, and 17 soil geochemical indicators were measured. Two geostatistical models (ordinary kriging, OK; regression kriging, RK) alongside four machine-learning algorithms: Elastic-Net, radial-basis-function support vector machine (RBF-SVM), Honest Random Forest (Honest RF), and XGBoost were benchmarked. We adopted a dual nested cross-validation scheme to separate model-fitting performance from spatial extrapolation capacity. The results indicated that our spatial‑block cross‑validation avoids inflated accuracy caused by random sample division. Among all competing models, Honest RF achieved the optimal performance, exhibiting minimal residual spatial aggregation and stable predictive performance for unmeasured watershed areas. Permutation feature importance (PFI) and non‑linear response curves consistently identify soil organic matter (SOM), lead (Pb), and mercury (Hg) as dominant correlative predictors closely associated with spatial variation in soil Se, with distinct threshold-saturation responses for each driving factor. We put forward a tentative tri‑element coupling hypothesis explaining Se–Hg–Pb co‑enrichment driven by rock weathering, atmospheric deposition and organic‑colloid interfacial reactions. Our combined analytical pipeline—multi‑model comparison, spatial cross‑validation and interpretable driver analysis—offers a practical reference for point-wise out-of-sample prediction of soil elements in mountain catchments with limited sample sizes.

science.title: Unravelling capacity fading in valve regulated lead acid battery pack for e-Rickshaw applications
science.description: This study investigates the electrical degradation behaviour of a 48 V valve-regulated lead–acid (VRLA) battery pack designed for e-rickshaw applications. The pack was subjected to continuous cycling under a severe duty profile derived from the IEC 63,193 standard, representing long-range operation under heavy load and steep-gradient driving conditions. The battery pack achieved peak performance corresponding to a maximum running time of approximately 162 min between cycles 110 and 150. However, after 164 cycles, the running time collapsed abruptly from 137 min to only 6 min, indicating sudden catastrophic failure. Several precursor warning signatures were identified prior to this collapse, including reduced charge acceptance, progressive suppression of rebound voltage, accelerated decline in energy efficiency, and a pronounced transformation of the discharge voltage profile. These degradation indicators consistently converged around the ~ 117th cycle, marking a clear inflection point at which aging transitioned from gradual to accelerated behaviour. The systematic evolution of the discharge voltage profile serve as a distinctive electrochemical fingerprint of positive active material (PAM) degradation. Based on these observations, a Dual-Regime Discharge behaviour is proposed to describe the transition from high-voltage-dominated discharge to low-voltage-dominated discharge as degradation progresses.
